items.title: Ray Bryant interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York City, New York, March 22, 1998
items.q: Jo Jones the drummer, he decided that he wanted to have a trio and he called me and I did that for a year

ctx.x: Did it come to a point where you felt you needed to go to New York? What prompted the move to New York?

Oh yeah, yeah, yeah. I was in Philadelphia and Carmen McRae came to town without a piano player, and I went and filled in with her. And when she left I left with her. I was with her for maybe two years and I came back to Philadelphia, and then Jo Jones, of Count Basie fame, Jo Jones the drummer, he decided that he wanted to have a trio and he called me and I did that for a year, still based in Philadelphia. Then I got back from the thing with Jo Jones and I said I’m working only with people from New York and I…

items.title: 68642_Jo Jones oral history interview
items.q: I had Ray Bryant and his brother and I said, now this is it.

ctx.x: So now then, '65, this is up to '70. You've been going back and forth to Europe.

You must remember, I came through Canada and Ray Bryant was playing with Carmen McCrae. I said, "You're fired." So I formed a trio for one year. I had it for 11 1/2 months. I had Ray Bryant and his brother and I said, now this is it. Then after I did that, then I left and I went to San Juan to open up Ochos Puertos, Hinton: Ochos Puertos. Eight Doors. There was a laundry there. It was one block from the Governor's mansion in old San Juan. I was in Pepi Alegria and I had a partner that understood about musicians…

One of the finest records I think I've ever heard of a trio, and one of the best recorded drum albums I've ever heard in my life, is the one that you made with Ray Bryant and his brother Tommy Bryant and you, called Jo Jones Plus Two.
